chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Ibn Mukkan, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in the mosque, he said, 'Stand up, so-and-so; stand up, so-and-so; stand up, so-and-so,' until he had sent out five men. Then he said, 'Exit from our mosque; do not pray in it, while you do not purify yourselves (by paying zakat).'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet expel men from the mosque according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the obligation of transferring zakat to the Imam, this hadith highlights the spiritual efficacy of zakat by linking it directly to the acceptance of prayer. The Prophet’s command for the five men to leave the mosque underscores the Shia scholarly view that zakat serves as a means of spiritual purification (tazkiyah), and its neglect renders one’s worship incomplete or less valid.
